extracted.intended_audience: literate London readers of a daily periodical (families, women, idle gentlemen / 'fraternity of Spectators')
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial mission and behavioral rules appearing in early-18th-century Spectator essays: guidance on the purpose, tone, audience, frequency, and the small-club rules reproduced in the paper. Focus is on producing short daily moral/witty essays for a general London readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine morality with wit
rubrics_metrics.description: “I shall endeavour to enliven Morality with Wit, and to temper Wit with Morality, that my Readers may, if possible, both Ways find their account in the Speculation of the Day.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make instruction agreeable and diversion useful; balance moral instruction and entertainment so readers gain both pleasure and improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily frequency and regularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper is distributed every morning (the Publisher reports 'Three Thousand of them distributed every Day') and the author promises to 'refresh their Memories from Day to Day' until vice and folly are remedied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish short, regular daily pieces intended to be read as part of morning routine (recommended as part of tea-time); maintain consistency to cultivate readers' habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for tea-time / short morning reading
rubrics_metrics.description: The author recommends the paper 'to all well-regulated Families, that set apart an Hour in every Morning for Tea and Bread and Butter' and advises that it be 'looked upon as a Part of the Tea Equipage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep pieces concise, accessible, and appropriate for brief morning consumption so they can be read and discussed during domestic morning routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audiences to address
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper is explicitly recommended to: (a) 'well-regulated Families', (b) the 'Fraternity of Spectators' (idle gentlemen, contemplative tradesmen, titular physicians, Fellows of the Royal Society, Templers not contentious, and statesmen out of business), (c) the 'Blanks of Society' who need daily intellectual material, and (d) 'the female World' to divert them from trifles and point out imperfections and virtues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor content to be useful and pleasing across these groups: instructive to families, entertaining and contemplative to idle gentlemen, forming conversational material for the socially uninformed, and corrective/enhancing for women readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring philosophy and serious thought into common places
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambition to 'bring Philosophy out of Closets and Libraries, Schools and Colleges, to dwell in Clubs and Assemblies, at Tea-tables, and in Coffee-houses.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate elevated ideas into plain, social contexts; make philosophical or moral points accessible to everyday readers in social settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inflaming hatreds and prejudices
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer writings 'that tend to the wearing out of Ignorance, Passion, and Prejudice' rather than those 'which naturally conduce to inflame Hatreds, and make Enmities irreconcileable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor conciliatory, educating content over polemical or inflammatory pieces; aim to reduce enmity and prejudice in readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial modesty and quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: The author promises 'to give it over as soon as I grow dull' and enters a 'Caveat against' the raillery of small wits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a commitment to quality—discontinue the publication or change approach if it ceases to be lively and useful; be self-aware of declining quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clubs are useful when founded for improvement or innocent relaxation
rubrics_metrics.description: Clubs 'when knit together, by Love of Society, not a Spirit of Faction, and do not meet to censure or annoy those that are absent, but to enjoy one another... for their own Improvement, or for the Good of others, or at least to relax themselves from the Business of the Day, by an innocent and chearful Conversation, there may be something very useful in these little Institutions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clubs positively if their purpose is social improvement, mutual instruction, or harmless relaxation; view factional or censorious clubs negatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-pence Club Rule I: Entrance fee
rubrics_metrics.description: I. Every Member at his first coming in shall lay down his Two Pence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership requires a small inaugural stake; establishes commitment and club fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-pence Club Rule II: personal pipe supply
rubrics_metrics.description: II. Every Member shall fill his Pipe out of his own Box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must provide for their own tobacco; enforces personal responsibility and hygiene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-pence Club Rule III: absence penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: III. If any Member absents himself he shall forfeit a Penny for the Use of the Club, unless in case of Sickness or Imprisonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalize unexcused absences to encourage attendance; exemptions only for sickness or imprisonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-pence Club Rule IV: profanity sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: IV. If any Member swears or curses, his Neighbour may give him a Kick upon the Shins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Socially enforce civility by permitting a corporal admonishment for foul language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-pence Club Rule V: falsehood penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: V. If any Member tells Stories in the Club that are not true, he shall forfeit for every third Lie an Half-Penny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage dishonesty in storytelling by small fines for repeated untruths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-pence Club Rule VI: assault liability
rubrics_metrics.description: VI. If any Member strikes another wrongfully, he shall pay his Club for him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make assailants financially liable for harms they cause within the club.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-pence Club Rule VII: spouse charges
rubrics_metrics.description: VII. If any Member brings his Wife into the Club, he shall pay for whatever she drinks or smoaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members bringing spouses must cover their consumption; discourages spouses' attendance or ensures they pay for themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-pence Club Rule VIII: manner of fetching spouse
rubrics_metrics.description: VIII. If any Member's Wife comes to fetch him Home from the Club, she shall speak to him without the Door.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulate privacy and decorum when members are retrieved by spouses; avoid domestic disturbance inside the room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-pence Club Rule IX: insult sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: IX. If any Member calls another Cuckold, he shall be turned out of the Club.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expel members who make serious personal insults (protect reputation and civility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-pence Club Rule X: trade exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: X. None shall be admitted into the Club that is of the same Trade with any Member of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibit admitting members sharing a trade with existing members—presumably to avoid competition, collusion, or dominance of one trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-pence Club Rule XI: tradesmanship privilege
rubrics_metrics.description: XI. None of the Club shall have his Cloaths or Shoes made or mended, but by a Brother Member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privileged internal economy: members should patronize fellow members for services, encouraging mutual support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-pence Club Rule XII: political/religious test
rubrics_metrics.description: XII. No Non-juror shall be capable of being a Member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership excludes 'Non-jurors' (those refusing oaths), imposing a political/religious loyalty test.
